thread:
alex: Quick sync — we need a final recommendation on Dedicated GPU reservation for eu-west pools. Customer SLAs ask for guaranteed sustained throughput (tokens/min) for enterprise Dedicated customers. Thinking about a conservative commit + burst runway for Q3. Any strong objections to 10% headroom + maintenance buffer?

maria: No objections. Can you post current observed sustained throughput patterns (p50/p95/p99) and seq length assumptions? need numbers to size.

kevin: From monitoring: typical sustained workload across customers in eu-west: p50 ~ 780k tokens/min, p95 ~ 1.4M tokens/min, p99 spikes ~ 2.1M tokens/min (short lived). Seq lengths vary, median ~384, tail 2048.

samir: Here’s a quick capacity calc I ran locally — share for sanity check:

```
Assumptions:
- GPU flavor: A100-80GB equivalent
- effective tokens/sec per GPU (sustained, median seq): ~430
- target committed throughput (sustained): 1.2M tokens/min -> 20k tokens/sec
- safety: 10% headroom + 5% maintenance overhead -> multiplier 1.15

Required GPUs = ceil( (20_000 * 1.15) / 430 ) = ceil(23_000 / 430) = ceil(53.49) = 54 GPUs
Round up to wallet-friendly increments -> 56 GPUs

Notes: if customers prefer better p95, bump to 72 GPUs to cover ~1.8M tokens/min sustained.
```

alex: That aligns with my napkin math. Important callouts: 1) reserved commit sizing affects monthly committed $ and billing cadence, 2) we should prefer even multiples across AZs to avoid cross-AZ egress hot spots, 3) hold a small shared burst pool to absorb p99 spikes.

kevin: +1. For cross-AZ we're seeing a 3-5% latency penalty if routing crosses zones during spikes. So prefer equal pinned capacity per AZ. If we do 56 GPUs, split 28/28 across two AZs.

maria: What about instance type mix? H100 gives better perf at higher cost. Any guidance on using mixed flavors to optimize cost/perf?

samir: Operationally mixed fleet complicates kernel selection & quantization paths. For customers with predictable steady throughput, H100 reserved makes sense. For general-purpose multi-tenant Dedicated pools, stick to one flavor per pool. We can offer a high-performance tier (H100) for premium customers.

ops-bot: Reservation consumption report: eu-west pool 'dedicated-eu-std' current reserved: 40 GPUs, active usage (7d median): 46 GPUs, 7d p95: 68 GPUs. Unbilled burst consumption: 12 GPUs (ephemeral).

alex: That report explains the gap — current reserved of 40 is under the p95 demand. Proposal: bump to 56 GPUs reserved for base commit, and maintain a 12 GPU burst buffer (shared burst pool) to cover p99 short spikes. This gives committed runway and reduces emergency overage charges.

kevin: Can we simulate the billing delta? rough numbers will help sales when pitching commit. Samir, do you have a quick per-GPU/month committed vs on-demand delta?

samir: ballpark: committed A100 per-GPU effective cost ~ 0.6x on-demand in our cloud contracts. So committing 16 extra GPUs buys ~40% more steady throughput at lower unit cost vs on-demand. But beware commitment term length (12/36mo) — we should size conservative + quarterly reviews.

maria: Action items: 1) alex to propose 56 GPU per eu-west Dedicated pool commit + 12 GPU shared burst (ops-owned) ; 2) kevin to model AZ split and overlay with maintenance windows; 3) samir to produce a short cost delta sheet for sales (committed vs on-demand) and risk notes.

alex: I'll draft the commit proposal and post to the capacity-runway doc. Meeting if needed tomorrow 09:30 UTC. Thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin: LGTM, tagging @maria for follow-up on customer-facing wording.

maria: Will sync with sales and legal on SLA language.

ops-bot: Note: filing cloud-billing ticket CB-7284 for historical overage in May that pushed-on demand costs. Recorded for review.
